newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: APN sees 1997 as year of consolidation.
newsitem.headline: APN sees 1997 as year of consolidation.

text.p: Regional newspaper and radio station operator Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it viewed its current calendar 1997 year as strengthening its operations and getting more value from acquisitions.
"The focus this year is on consolidation and extracting value from acquisitions," APN chief executive Cameron O'Reilly told an analysts' briefing.
Earlier the group reported a 12.6 percent rise in pre-abnormal net profit to A$12.6 million for the first half ended June 30.
O'Reilly said restructuring and rationalisation continued at Radio Network of New Zealand group with staff reductions of 100 expected this year and a similar number in 1988.
The second half was however expected to be better for results than the traditionally flat first six months, he said.
In outdoor advertising, Buspak's revenue for the year to date was up 16 percent, he said.
"Asia will show us good opportunities for (Buspak) growth in the next three years," O'Reilly said.
He expected a strong finish for the year from outdoor advertising while the turnaround in specialist publishing was continuing.
Internet publishing was expected to benefit the group in the next three to five years, O'Reilly said.
APN is about 49 percent owned by Irish media group Independent Newspapers Plc and the family interests of Irish businessman Tony O'Reilly.
